pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/19665

The background task now runs for the lifetime of `Http2Stream`. A resettable task source is used to indicate that the response has finished writing.

~A change here is the response data pipe is reset inside the background task. This is done so that the task can go back to waiting on `pipeReader.ReadAsync` for content from the next stream to start.~

A second resettable task source is used to pause ProcessDataTask until the output producer is reset.

Before
```
|       Method |     Mean |    Error |   StdDev |     Op/s | Gen 0 | Gen 1 | Gen 2 | Allocated |
|------------- |---------:|---------:|---------:|---------:|------:|------:|------:|----------:|
| EmptyRequest | 30.80 us | 0.589 us | 0.723 us | 32,466.9 |     - |     - |     - |     651 B |
```

After
```
|       Method |     Mean |    Error |   StdDev |     Op/s | Gen 0 | Gen 1 | Gen 2 | Allocated |
|------------- |---------:|---------:|---------:|---------:|------:|------:|------:|----------:|
| EmptyRequest | 28.21 us | 0.561 us | 0.873 us | 35,452.3 |     - |     - |     - |     415 B |
```

issue_context.title: HTTP2: Remove per request async state machine allocation
issue_context.body:
Http2OutputProducer.ProcessDataWrites is a background task that is called once per stream:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/303201/76045788-f65ff780-5fc2-11ea-9011-462e3984fb3c.png)

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/7aaad9dde22a699a3c8d991547c6551fbdbf43c3/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Internal/Http2/Http2OutputProducer.cs#L373

Once Http2MessageBody is reused the state machine it will be the only per-request HTTP/2 allocation.

review_comments: Nit: move these methods below constructor.
This assert should be checking the _responseCompleteTaskSource  status is completed. Essentially the _responseCompleteTaskSource  should have been completed by then.
Lets get rid of the disposal altogether.

So the loop in the background task will be `do { } while (true);`

I'll add a comment that it is never exited and will "stop" when the state machine is garbage collected along with Http2OutputProducer.

I think it will be a problem

Leak from IAsyncEnumerable which has `ValueTask<T> MoveNextAsync()`

https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/39321
Toub mentioned making `s_currentActiveTasks` a weak table. It is currently still a dictionary: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/search?q=s_currentActiveTasks&unscoped_q=s_currentActiveTasks
I agree with @halter73 that avoiding a little complexity around Dispose isn't worth memory leaks when built as debug.
If Dispose is called, you would be resetting a field in an already disposed object.
This object isn't disposed, it'll just reset the awaitable which is harmless.
Why can't we use the version of this in the runtime? https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/src/libraries/Common/tests/System/Threading/Tasks/Sources/ManualResetValueTaskSource.cs

Its in a runtime test project.

Or are you saying you want to automatically mirror that file to our repo? That seems like overkill for a simple type.
